status.value: Full Medi-Cal + full dental — and no change to the plan or premiums in 2027
status.detail: DHCS status table: January 2026 "Full Medi-Cal + full Dental"; January 2027 "Keep Managed Care Plan"; July 2027 "Keep full Medi-Cal + full Dental" and "Don't pay premium." If you are also a California permanent resident, the LPR rows also apply to you as a citizen, and the citizen row is the simpler one.

status.item: Lawful permanent resident who completed the five-year waiting period (or is exempt from it)
status.value: Full Medi-Cal + full dental, federally funded; keep your managed care plan; no premium
status.detail: DHCS status table: January 2026 "Full Medi-Cal + full Dental"; January 2027 "Keep Managed Care Plan"; July 2027 "Keep full Medi-Cal + full Dental" and "Don't pay premium." The difference from the row below is the five-year waiting period: DHCS describes the group still inside it as people "who are in the five-year waiting period before they can get full-scope federal Medicaid."

status.item: Lawful permanent resident still inside the five-year waiting period
status.value: Full Medi-Cal + full dental (state-funded) in 2026; Fee-for-Service from January 2027; a monthly premium from July 2027
status.detail: DHCS status table: January 2026 "Full Medi-Cal + full Dental"; January 2027 "Move to Fee-for-Service"; July 2027 "(Age 21 and older and not pregnant) Keep full Medi-Cal and move to emergency only dental" and "(Age 21-59 and not pregnant) Must pay premium to keep Medi-Cal." California funds this coverage; the federal government does not, because the five-year bar has not been satisfied. DHCS's change calendar describes this group as "some people with green cards who are in the five-year waiting period before they can get full-scope federal Medicaid."

status.item: Everyone else without a qualifying immigration status
status.value: Adults 19+ cannot newly enroll in full-scope Medi-Cal as of January 1, 2026
status.detail: "Starting on Jan. 1, 2026, adults without a qualifying immigration status can no longer enroll in full Medi-Cal. If you were already enrolled before that date, you can keep your coverage, as long as you remain eligible — make sure to renew during your renewal month." Children 0–18 and pregnant people keep full-scope coverage regardless of status.

changes.value: Some adults can no longer sign up for full-scope Medi-Cal because of immigration status
changes.detail: If you already have full-scope Medi-Cal you can keep it regardless of status, as long as you renew on time and still meet Medi-Cal rules. If your Medi-Cal ends you have three months to sign up again; if you miss that, you can only get restricted-scope Medi-Cal (emergency care, pregnancy care, nursing home care).

changes.item: October 2026 — federal reclassification of certain statuses
changes.value: State-funded full-scope Medi-Cal until June 30, 2027 for affected people
changes.detail: Affected groups listed by DHCS: refugees and asylees, humanitarian parolees, and survivors of domestic violence or human trafficking with a pending case. From July 1, 2027 these groups "will only be able to get pregnancy-related care and emergency services." Permanent residents are not in this group.

changes.value: Some members move from a health plan to fee-for-service
changes.detail: Applies to people who are undocumented, some green card holders in the five-year waiting period, and people considered Permanently Residing in the U.S. Under Color of Law. "Fee-for-Service does not mean you pay. Medi-Cal still pays for your care." Enhanced Care Management and Community Supports are plan-only services and do not continue in FFS.

changes.item: July 1, 2027 — dental coverage and monthly premiums
changes.value: Some members lose full dental or must pay a monthly premium
changes.detail: If you do not pay the premium, "your Medi-Cal will change to restricted-scope, which covers: Emergency care; Pregnancy-related care; Nursing home care." Children, pregnant people, and former foster youth under 26 are exempt from the premium and keep full dental.

changes.value: Federal Medicaid money may only cover citizens, permanent residents, Cuban/Haitian entrants and COFA residents
changes.detail: Section 71109 bars federal Medicaid funding for people who are residents of the U.S. but fall outside those four categories, and extends the bar to CHIP. It also ends federal Medicaid funding for refugees and asylees (who can qualify as permanent residents after one year). A lawful permanent resident is inside the categories that keep funding, so this provision does not cut you off; it is the federal rule behind the state-funded full-scope coverage California offers certain other groups until June 30, 2027.

work-rule.value: The work rule applies "regardless of immigration status" to the MAGI New Adult Group
work-rule.detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30, page 1. California law codifies this: WIC § 14005.69(b)(1)(B) includes state-funded Medi-Cal adults who meet the same criteria as the ACA adult group.

work-rule.value: Your status does not exempt you; the $580 income test and the 80-hour options are the same for everyone
work-rule.detail: The rule operates on the coverage group and the individual's circumstances, not on immigration status.
Disability/medically frail, caregiving, pregnancy, CalFresh or CalWORKs compliance, tribal membership, veteran with a total disability, foster youth, high-unemployment county.

marketplace.item: Green card holders and Covered California financial help in 2027
marketplace.detail: Covered California lists lawful permanent residents (green card holders), Cuban and Haitian entrants, and Compact of Free Association migrants as the groups that remain eligible for financial help in 2027.

marketplace.value: "Covered California and Medi-Cal use the same application"
marketplace.detail: When you apply, "we check whether you may qualify for both programs, no matter your immigration status." List everyone in your household regardless of status, because household size and income drive the calculation.

marketplace.value: "Applying will not affect your immigration status or your chances of becoming a lawful permanent resident or U.S. citizen."
